prerequisites: Having completed the Basic Electronics course is recommended.
Prior knowledge of electronics and algebra is required.
It would be convenient for the student to have acquired basic competencies in Electronics and Mathematical Foundations.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals and applications of digital electronics and microprocessors.
Ability to design analog, digital, and power electronic systems.

Know the electronic components commonly used in digital electronics, their behavior, characterization, and representation in electronic diagrams and schematics, as well as their practical limitations.
Understand the topology of the most common digital circuits, their structure, operation, and applications.
Know the electronic devices used in solving engineering problems.
Become familiar with the technical language of digital electronics.
Know the fundamentals for the analysis of digital electronic systems.
Understand the principles for the design of digital electronic circuits, both with discrete and integrated elements, including programmable devices.
Know the basic computer tools for simulating digital electronic systems.
Become familiar with the scientific method in circuit analysis and design.
Know traditional and new technology information sources applied to digital electronics.
Recognize, analyze, design, simulate, assemble, and test, through direct measurements, digital electronic circuits of basic and medium complexity.
Prepare individual and group assignments, developing critical capacity to discuss obtained results and compare experimental conclusions with theoretical knowledge.
Perform supervised laboratory practices, analyze collected data, and prepare lab reports.
Use basic laboratory instruments (oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, signal generators) and assembly systems.
Develop collaborative work competencies through small group practices and projects.
Design digital circuits using programmable devices and simulation tools.
Integrate knowledge and skills in the development and presentation of projects related to real applications.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Number systems and Boolean algebra
2.2. Implementation of switching functions with Logic Gates.
4.4. Microprocessor circuits for industrial and power instrumentation.
Practice 4: Real application of a microcontroller.
teaching_methods: Exercises and demonstrations with simulation and industrial tools
Autonomous and group work based on Project-Based Learning
Assimilation of knowledge derived from theoretical classes
Resolution of exercises proposed in participatory lectures
Resolution of practical cases proposed in laboratory practices
Elaboration of laboratory practice reports through group work
Development and presentation of a project related to real challenges and topic 4 of the subject.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.20 * Lab reports + 0.6 * Exam + 0.2 * Project development and presentation. A minimum score of 5 points out of 10 is required for each activity (each lab report, each part of the exam, and the project). Lab attendance is mandatory, and students with more than 10% non-attendance will be marked as 'not qualified' for practices. For the extraordinary call, the evaluation structure is similar, but the 20% dedicated to practices varies based on prior attendance, either through resubmission of reports or a combination of simulation reports and a lab exam. For single evaluation, the final grade is 0.1 * Simulation reports + 0.25 * Lab exam + 0.65 * Theoretical/practical exam, with a minimum of 5 points in each part. All evaluation methods can be performed virtually if health authorities advise.
